topics.title: Why Is the School Answer for How Planes Fly Wrong?

demand.title: What Makes an Airplane Fly | 3D Animation

topics.hook: Most of us were taught why a wing lifts a plane. NASA says that answer is wrong.
topics.angle: Cutaway of an A380 wing in a wind tunnel of glowing streamlines. The school answer: air over the longer top must hurry to meet the air underneath (equal transit). Show two air parcels split at the leading edge: the top one arrives first, not together, so the premise fails; a flat paper plane and a symmetric wing still lift. The real step: the wing at an angle turns the airflow downward, faster flow and lower pressure above, the air is pushed down and the wing is pushed up. Payoff (computed by code from the two Airbus figures): each square metre of an A380's wing holds up about 680 kg at take-off, a small car on every square metre. Loop back to the wing.

topics.title: How Was the Golden Gate Bridge's Cable Spun in the Air, One Wire at a Time?

demand.title: How Humans Mastered Bridge Building

topics.hook: Each of the Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables is almost a metre thick. Nobody lifted it into place.
topics.angle: Cutaway of a main cable over the tower saddle. The mechanism: spinning wheels run back and forth between the anchorages on a cable, each trip laying a pencil-thin steel wire, 0.192 in, across the strait; wires are bundled into 61 strands, then squeezed round and wrapped. Dive from the bridge to the cable cross-section to a single wire with its scale badge. Payoff (computed by code from the sourced facts): the 80,000 miles of wire in both cables would wrap round the Earth's equator about 3 times. Loop back to the cable on the tower.

topics.title: How Does a Bathroom Outlet Know to Cut the Power Before It Hurts You?

demand.title: How Electrical Outlets Work 🤔

topics.hook: The outlet by your sink is counting every bit of current that leaves it, and every bit that comes back.
topics.angle: Cutaway of a GFCI outlet beside a sink, opened in 3D. Current goes out on the hot wire and comes back on the neutral; both pass through one small ring (a sensing coil). Equal and opposite, the ring feels nothing. A hair dryer drops in water: some current finds a new path home through water and a person, so less comes back; the ring now feels the difference, a tiny coil voltage wakes the chip, a solenoid snaps the contacts open. Payoff by code from the two OSHA figures: it notices a gap of about 5 thousandths of an amp and cuts the power in 25 thousandths of a second (1000 / 40). Then the TEST button: it simply makes that leak on purpose. Loop back to the ring.
topics.why_now: The niche's most-viewed on-profile gadget Short this quarter: Zack D. Films' 'How Electrical Outlets Work' has 77.3M views in 31 days, above its 29.8M subscribers, still adding 2.5M a day. We tell one part it doesn't: the safety outlet everyone has pressed TEST on. A gadget_inside topic (low tier in our recipe, 'only for a strong topic'): this is one.

topics.title: How Does a Pellet the Size of a Fingertip Match a Ton of Coal?

demand.title: Most Important Invention, Part 9: Nuclear Power Plant

topics.hook: This ceramic pellet is smaller than your fingertip. It makes as much energy as a ton of coal.
topics.angle: Cutaway run through a pressurised-water plant, following the heat. One pellet in a fuel rod; a neutron splits a uranium atom, the pieces fly apart and heat the pellet; water under pressure carries the heat away without boiling, a steam generator boils a second loop, steam spins the turbine, the generator makes the power; cooling tower releases only water vapour. Side by side at true size: the pellet next to a ton of coal (DOE). Payoff by code from DOE figures: US reactors made about 782 billion kWh in 2024 from 94 reactors, so one reactor about 8.3 billion kWh a year; running more than 92% of the time. Loop back to the pellet.

topics.title: NVIDIA's First Chip Drew 3D Without Triangles, and Nobody Used It

demand.title: NVIDIA's First Chip

topics.hook: NVIDIA's first chip drew 3D with curves instead of triangles. Almost no game used it.
topics.angle: Open on the NV1 board (Diamond Edge 3D, 1995: graphics, sound and Sega Saturn controller ports on one card). Inside the chip: a curved patch bent into a 3D shape (quadratic texture mapping) next to the triangle mesh everyone else used. Microsoft's DirectX (Sept 1995) is built around triangles; developers don't write for curves; NVIDIA is struggling to stay in business. The pivot: NV3, the RIVA 128 (1997), triangles, 3.5 million transistors, made in 350 nm. Payoff by code: NVIDIA's newest GPU, Rubin, has 336 billion transistors, about 1.3 million times the NV1's 250 thousand. Loop back to the curved patch. Say 'about 250 thousand' (the source says approximately). No 'nearly bankrupt' or 'thirty days' line: the sources say only 'struggling to stay in business' with 'greatly reduced staff'.
topics.why_now: True Campside Stories' 'NVIDIA's First Chip' Short has 1.78M views on a 29.8K channel (60x), the biggest on-profile breakout in this week's market scan (+12K views an hour). Chip history, our core lane, and no chip-history Short in the feed.

topics.title: What a chatbot does to write one word: chop the text into tokens, then run every token through all 70 billion numbers

demand.title: What Happens Inside an AI Chip When You Ask a Question

topics.hook: Before a chatbot writes one word, it does billions of multiplications. Here is every step.
topics.angle: Zoom in from a typed question on a phone screen: the sentence is cut into tokens (about 4 characters each, about three quarters of a word; OpenAI), each token becomes a row in a 128K-entry vocabulary (Meta Llama 3), then a list of numbers. Zoom into the model: the token's numbers pass through every layer, each of the 70 billion parameters does one multiply-and-add (2 operations per parameter, Kaplan et al. 2020), out comes a score for every token in the vocabulary, one is picked, appended, and the whole pass runs again for the next token. Payoff by code: 2 x 70 billion = about 140 billion operations for one token; a 75-word answer is about 100 tokens (OpenAI), so about 14 trillion operations. Loop back to the next word appearing on the phone. Name the model as Meta's Llama 3 70B (an open model with published figures), never 'ChatGPT's size' (OpenAI doesn't publish it). Tag the layers 'illustration'.
topics.why_now: How AI works and how the internet works are core lanes in profile.md, but both formats are long-only and the Shorts feed had no AI topic at all (19 open: chips, machines, history, power). zoom_inside is the Short format that can tell it; its reference (1.02M views on a 12.7K channel, 80.6x) is this exact idea: what the hardware does when you ask a question.
